Find the statement that is not correct.
(2) True — low grade copper ores are leached with acid or bacteria and the copper displaced
with scrap iron; that is hydrometallurgy.
(3) True — the puddling furnace, lined with haematite, oxidises the carbon and other impurities
out of cast iron to give wrought iron.
(4) True — in vapour phase refining the metal must form a volatile compound that can be
distilled off and then decomposed, as in the Mond process for nickel and the van Arkel method
for titanium.
(1) False — a collector does the **opposite** of enhancing wettability. In froth flotation the
collector (pine oil, fatty acids, xanthates) coats the mineral particles and makes them
water-repellent, so they attach to the air bubbles and rise with the froth, while the gangue
stays wetted and sinks.
If the collector made the ore more wettable it would sink with the gangue and the separation
would fail.
∴ statement (1) is not correct.

kcet|Chemistry|2014|55||0|0:
The volume given is that of one CsCl ion pair, and the question says this equals the volume
of a cube whose side is the Cs–Cs distance.
So simply take the cube root:
a³ = 7.014 × 10⁻²³ cm³
Write it so the exponent divides by three:
a³ = 70.14 × 10⁻²⁴ cm³
a = (70.14)^(1/3) × (10⁻²⁴)^(1/3)
(70.14)^(1/3) ≈ 4.12, since 4³ = 64 and 4.2³ = 74
(10⁻²⁴)^(1/3) = 10⁻⁸
a ≈ 4.12 × 10⁻⁸ cm
Convert to ångström, remembering 1 Å = 10⁻⁸ cm:
a ≈ 4.12 Å
Of the values offered this is nearest 4 Å.
∴ about 4 Å.
kcet|Chemistry|2014|58||0|0:
Both oxides are basic and each needs two moles of HCl:
BaO + 2HCl ⇒ BaCl₂ + H₂O
CaO + 2HCl ⇒ CaCl₂ + H₂O
Total acid used:
n(HCl) = 0.100 L × 2.5 mol L⁻¹ = 0.25 mol
Let the mass of BaO be x g, so CaO is (10 − x) g. Molar masses: BaO = 153, CaO = 56.
2(x/153) + 2((10 − x)/56) = 0.25
Divide through by 2:
x/153 + (10 − x)/56 = 0.125
Multiply by 153 × 56 = 8568:
56x + 153(10 − x) = 1071
56x + 1530 − 153x = 1071
−97x = −459
x = 4.73 g of BaO
So CaO = 10 − 4.73 = 5.27 g
percentage of CaO = (5.27/10) × 100 = 52.7%
∴ approximately 52.6%.
kcet|Chemistry|2013|1||0|0:
Zone refining relies on one fact: impurities are more soluble in the **molten** metal than in
the solid.
A circular heater is moved slowly along a rod of the metal, melting a narrow zone. As the zone
travels, the metal crystallising behind it is pure and the impurities stay dissolved in the melt
and are carried along to one end, which is then cut off.
Repeating the pass gives metal of extremely high purity.
The method is used where that purity really matters — for the semiconductors **germanium**
and silicon, and for gallium and indium, where even parts per billion of impurity would ruin
the electrical properties.
Aluminium is refined electrolytically (Hoope's process), copper by electrolysis, and silver by
cupellation or the Parkes process.
∴ germanium.

kcet|Chemistry|2013|2||0|0.s:
Convert mass to moles, then moles to molecules.
Molar mass of water = 2(1) + 16 = 18 g mol⁻¹
moles = mass / molar mass = 0.018 / 18 = 0.001 mol = 10⁻³ mol
Number of molecules = moles × Avogadro's number
= 10⁻³ × 6.022 × 10²³
= 6.022 × 10²⁰
A neat way to see it: 0.018 g is exactly one thousandth of a mole, so the count is Avogadro's
number divided by a thousand, which drops the exponent by 3 from 23 to 20.
The distractors are simply this answer with the exponent moved.
∴ 6.022 × 10²⁰ molecules.

kcet|Chemistry|2013|3||0|0:
The molecular formula is a whole-number multiple of the empirical formula.
Empirical formula mass of CH₂O:
12 + 2(1) + 16 = 30
Find the multiplier:
n = molecular mass / empirical formula mass = 90 / 30 = 3
Multiply every subscript by 3:
(CH₂O)₃ = C₃H₆O₃
Check: 3(12) + 6(1) + 3(16) = 36 + 6 + 48 = 90 ✓
Note that C₆H₁₂O₆, option (3), has mass 180, which would be n = 6 — that is glucose, not this
compound. C₃H₆O₃ is lactic acid.
∴ C₃H₆O₃.
kcet|Chemistry|2013|4||0|0:
Count the σ bonds on a carbon atom in each allotrope; that gives the number of hybrid orbitals.
Graphite — each carbon is bonded to three others in flat hexagonal sheets. Three σ bonds and
no lone pair means three hybrid orbitals, so **sp²**, with bond angles of 120°. The fourth
electron stays in an unhybridised p orbital, and these delocalise across the sheet, which is why
graphite conducts electricity and feels slippery.
Diamond — each carbon is bonded to four others in a rigid three-dimensional network. Four σ
bonds means four hybrid orbitals, so **sp³**, with bond angles of 109°28′. Every valence
electron is locked into a σ bond, so diamond is an insulator and the hardest natural substance.
The question asks for graphite first, then diamond.
∴ sp², sp³.

kcet|Chemistry|2013|5||0|0.s:
At STP one mole of any gas occupies 22400 cm³ (22.4 L).
First convert the volume to moles:
moles = 112 / 22400 = 0.005 mol
Molar mass of NH₃ = 14 + 3(1) = 17 g mol⁻¹
mass = moles × molar mass
= 0.005 × 17
= 0.085 g
Keep the units consistent — 112 cm³ is 0.112 L, and 0.112/22.4 gives the same 0.005 mol.
The distractors are this answer shifted by powers of ten, so the arithmetic of the exponent is
where the marks are lost.
∴ 0.085 g.

kcet|Chemistry|2013|6||0|0.s:
The structure is CH₃–CH(OH)–CH₂–CH(CH₃)–COOH.
Step 1 — find the principal functional group. –COOH outranks –OH, so the compound is named
as an acid and the OH becomes a 'hydroxy' prefix.
Step 2 — the chain must include the carboxyl carbon, and that carbon is always C1.
Numbering from the COOH:
C1 = COOH
C2 = CH bearing the CH₃ branch
C3 = CH₂
C4 = CH bearing the OH
C5 = CH₃
Five carbons in the chain ⇒ pentanoic acid.
Step 3 — cite the substituents alphabetically: hydroxy before methyl.
So it is 4-hydroxy-2-methylpentanoic acid.
Numbering from the other end would put the acid at C5, which is not allowed.
∴ 4-hydroxy 2 methyl pentanoic acid.

kcet|Chemistry|2013|7||0|0:
A negative standard **reduction** potential means the reverse process — oxidation — is the
favourable one. The species prefers to lose electrons rather than gain them.
For the alkali metals these values are strongly negative:
Li⁺ + e⁻ ⇒ Li, E° = −3.05 V
Na⁺ + e⁻ ⇒ Na, E° = −2.71 V
K⁺ + e⁻ ⇒ K, E° = −2.93 V
So in practice the metal gives its electron away:
Na ⇒ Na⁺ + e⁻
A species that donates electrons to something else reduces that other species, so it is acting
as a **reducing agent**, and is itself oxidised.
The more negative the potential the stronger the reducing agent, which is why lithium is the
strongest of all in aqueous solution.
An oxidising agent (1) would be the opposite, with a large positive E°, as fluorine has at +2.87 V.
∴ reducing agents.
